en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Mañjiṭṭhaka Mansion in the Itthivimāna Section
3. The Story of the Nāga’s Mansion “Adorned with jewels and gold,
covered with a great golden lattice;”
Having mounted a well-prepared, excellent elephant,
he came here through the air across the sky.
He was fashioned upon the two tusks of that elephant.
The lotus ponds with their clear waters are in full bloom;
amidst the lotuses, throngs of musical instruments resound,
and these enchanting women dance.
O lady of great majesty, you have attained divine power;
while still a human being, what merit did you perform?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing splendor?
"And your complexion shines in all directions.
"Having approached Bārāṇasī,
I gave a pair of garments to the Buddha;
Having bowed at his feet, I sat upon the ground;
filled with devotion, I joined my palms in reverence.
And the Buddha, whose skin was like refined gold—
He taught the impermanence of the origin of suffering;
he taught the unconditioned eternity of the cessation of suffering,
and he taught the path by which one may understand it.
Having had a short life and passed away from there, I,
possessing great renown, was reborn among the hosts of the Thirty-three;
I am one of the consorts of Sakka.
“Yasuttarā by name, renowned throughout the quarters.
Thus ends the third Nāga-vimāna.
